Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace instructions and the two required skills, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and parent policy before designing the single candidate. I’m using the wake-visual skill to interpret both required 3D views and the fish-control bookshelf because this is the mandated first architecture proposal from the naive seed.

The inherited guidance already records a semantic plateau: three completed static/restart descendants remain finite but lose the tight-return topology. I’m now comparing all four sampled policies and their measurements, with special attention to the best scalar rollout and the closest-approach rollout, so the new mechanism is distinguished from another static bend or gain retune.

The visual comparison and inherited logs agree on the failure mode: the recent policies are self-propelled and numerically stable, but settle into broad, powered loops with nearly parked joints. The only surviving positive scaffold is the earlier two-sided anterior phase-balanced regulator (`1.175L` minimum); requested-half-cycle energy, posterior phase/energy, static release, and force-selected posterior reinforcement all failed. I’m therefore restoring that scaffold and testing one new response topology: posterior damping only during measured hydrodynamic impulses that rotate translational course away from the target.

The bookshelf’s separation of slow route error from fast hydrodynamic response directly shapes this edit: target/course geometry remains the slow selector, while force is used only to veto an outward-producing posterior stroke. The failed parent reinforced “helpful” force with positive work; this candidate instead applies bounded negative work during harmful force, leaving the established mean bend and lag unchanged. I’m recording that hypothesis and its falsification boundary before touching the policy.

The candidate now differs from the proven `1.175L` scaffold only by three owned response parameters and one terminal posterior damping term; all geometry, anterior activity regulation, mean curvature, phase lag, braking, and command limits are unchanged. I’ve also revised the durable guidance to close the stale half-cycle/extra-tail-energy branch and record the negative force-reinforcement result. Next I’m running the mandated checks plus deterministic sign, locality, and symmetry probes—no CFD.

The mandated guidance check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker cannot identify a unique parent. I’m removing only that duplicated marker, then rerunning the check; this does not alter the experiment or candidate.

The first replay harness hit a Julia soft-scope issue before producing any result; the policy itself was not implicated. I’m rerunning the same read-only probe inside a function so it can complete cleanly.

The frozen replay confirms the implementation semantics on all 18,182 states of the useful `1.175L` rollout: the new term is negligible beyond `3L`, material inside `1.5L`, active on 62.3% of close states, performs no positive incremental joint work, and has zero lateral-reflection residual. It is exactly inactive at the inherited minimum because that instantaneous force is not outward—consistent with response selection rather than a hidden proximity impulse.

All required sanity checks now pass: material guidance/notes, lightweight Julia contract, 51/51 parameter-schema ownership, reflection/boundedness probes, and solver editable-boundary validation. The candidate remains the only editable policy artifact, and no CFD rollout was run.

Implemented exactly one candidate: bounded posterior damping during outward hydrodynamic impulses, built on the proven anterior phase-balanced scaffold.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:138)

All required checks pass, including the 51-field parameter schema, policy contract, reflection/boundedness probes, material guidance update, and editable-boundary validation. No formal CFD was run.
